title: Information Technology Act, 2000 — Section 6 (Use of Electronic Records and Signatures in Government)

content.overview: Section 6 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 enables the use of electronic records and electronic signatures in Government and its agencies. Where any law provides for filing of forms, applications or documents, issue or grant of licence, permit, sanction or approval, or receipt or payment of money in a particular manner, such requirement may be satisfied by electronic form as prescribed, and the appropriate Government may prescribe the manner and format of electronic filing and the method of payment.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Is a Government filing, licence or payment in issue? (2) Has the appropriate Government prescribed electronic manner/format? (3) Was the electronic path followed?
content.study:
s. 6 is enabling for e-governance. Prescription by the appropriate Government is typically required for the electronic mode to be valid under this section.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: E-governance enabling
sections.body: Filing, applications, licences, permits, sanctions, approvals and receipt/payment of money may be done in electronic form as provided.

sections.heading: Prescription
sections.body: Appropriate Government may prescribe manner and format of electronic filing and method of payment.

sections.heading: Legal satisfaction
sections.body: Where electronic mode is duly prescribed and followed, the statutory filing/issue/payment requirement is treated as satisfied under the section's scheme.

sections.heading: Link to ss. 4–5
sections.body: Recognition of electronic records and signatures underpins Government electronic processes authorised under s. 6.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Identify the Government act; check prescription; confirm compliance with electronic manner/format.

provisions.title: Use of electronic records and electronic signatures in Government and its agencies

examples.title: Online licence application
examples.body: Where the appropriate Government has prescribed electronic filing for a licence, an application filed in that format under s. 6 satisfies the filing requirement subject to the prescription.

hypotheticals.question: Can any citizen force a department to accept only paper if e-filing is prescribed?
hypotheticals.analysis: Where s. 6 and the prescription authorise electronic filing, the electronic mode is legally available; residual paper rules depend on the specific prescription and other law.

distinctions.title: s. 6 Government use vs s. 4 general recognition
distinctions.left: Enables prescribed electronic Government filings, licences and payments.
distinctions.right: General legal recognition of electronic records for writing requirements.

misconceptions.trap: s. 6 automatically digitises every Government process without notification.
misconceptions.correction: Electronic manner and format typically depend on prescription by the appropriate Government.
